references.text: Jesus compares his revelation to lightning that flashes from one end of the sky to the other—the day of the Son of Man will be unmistakable ([ref:Luk 17:24|Luke 17:24]).
The immediate context compares the days of the Son of Man with the days of Noah, when people lived as usual until judgment came ([ref:Luk 17:26-27|Luke 17:26-27]).
The parallel with Lot's days in Sodom—people ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and built, but on the day Lot left, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven ([ref:Luk 17:28-29|Luke 17:28-29]).

The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, where the Lord caused fire and sulfur to rain down—the historical example Jesus refers to in the context of his revelation ([ref:1 Mos 19:24-25|Genesis 19:24-25]).
Jesus uses the same comparison with Noah's days in Matthew's account: just as it was in the days of Noah, so will it be when the Son of Man comes ([ref:Matt 24:37-39|Matthew 24:37-39]).
The coming of the Son of Man is compared to lightning that goes from east to west—his revelation will be sudden and visible to all ([ref:Matt 24:27|Matthew 24:27]).
Paul describes the revelation (ἀποκάλυψις) of the Lord Jesus from heaven with his mighty angels in flaming fire—the same term used in Luke 17:30 ([ref:2 Tess 1:7-8|2 Thessalonians 1:7-8]).

Peter urges us to set our hope fully on the grace that will be brought at the revelation (ἀποκάλυψις) of Jesus Christ, the same word used for the day of the Son of Man ([ref:1 Pet 1:13|1 Peter 1:13]).

Paul speaks of waiting for the revelation (ἀποκάλυψις) of our Lord Jesus Christ—the same Greek word used in [ref:Luk 17:30|Luke 17:30] regarding the day of the Son of Man ([ref:1 Kor 1:7|1 Corinthians 1:7]).
Jesus warns that that day will come unexpectedly like a trap on all who live on the earth—the same theme of sudden revelation ([ref:Luk 21:34-35|Luke 21:34-35]).

The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night; while people say "peace and safety", sudden destruction comes—parallel to the unexpected revelation in Luke 17:30 ([ref:1 Tess 5:2-3|1 Thessalonians 5:2-3]).
The day of the Lord will come like a thief, and the elements will melt with fire—the fire motif recalls the Sodom parallel and the sudden revelation of the Son of Man ([ref:2 Pet 3:10|2 Peter 3:10]).
